title: Google begins certifying Registered App Stores for Android, but not in the US
gist: Google opened applications for its Registered App Stores program for Android outside the US and Europe, charging $10,000 per year, going live December 1 and requiring Android 17 QPR2, which many devices in target regions may never receive.

insights.claim: Google's Registered App Stores program is the voluntary international replacement for the court-ordered US remedy of hosting rival stores inside Google Play, after the Epic settlement was withdrawn when the court signaled it would not approve it.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Epic litigation produced a split regime: court order in the US, Google-controlled certification abroad.
insights.locator: Paragraphs beginning "The Android Registered App Stores program was initially"

insights.claim: Approved stores get one-click installs and silent background updates like Google Play, but must meet IP, illegal-content, privacy and ongoing security requirements.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Preferential install friction is the carrot that makes certification valuable to third-party stores.

insights.claim: Participation costs $10,000 per year, payable before review, plus possible extra review fees if malware issues arise.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: A fixed fee favors well-capitalized stores over small ones; Google gets a new revenue line and control over the gate.
insights.quote: It costs $10,000 per year to participate

insights.claim: The program goes live December 1 across dozens of countries outside the US and Europe, but only on Android 17 QPR2 or newer, so many devices in those regions may never get a compatible update.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Slow OEM update cycles limit real reach, blunting competitive impact on Google Play.

insights.claim: In the US the only alternative store listed in Google Play so far is Aptoide.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Court-ordered US store competition has had minimal uptake so far.
insights.locator: Paragraph beginning "Registered App Stores are still happening"
